decisions.decision: Does the mise tool declare its edge to cli?
decisions.ruling: Yes. mise gets depends = ["cli"], because its three shell-init templates read projects_dir from .all.cli.

decisions.decision: How does a <% %> expression sit inside a [mise.*] string?
decisions.ruling: The expression sits inside a TOML basic string ("..."), and each string literal inside it is a Go raw string in backticks, never a double quote, so the TOML string needs no escape. The engine renders a tools.toml that holds <% before it generates (P08 D6), so the generated mise file holds the rendered value.
decisions.rejected: Double quotes with TOML escapes inside the action; a TOML literal string.

decisions.decision: Which mise files does the mise tool still ship?
decisions.ruling: ~/.config/mise/config.toml and ~/.config/mise/miserc.toml stay shipped files of the mise tool, byte for byte with the new header. They are the user-level mise config, the Mac twin of the repo exception .config/mise.toml.tmpl, and config.toml has the top-level key min_version that no [mise.*] section holds. Only the old conf.d fragment mise.toml becomes [mise.*] tables.
decisions.rejected: Move config.toml into [mise.*] tables; drop miserc.toml (env_conf_d) now, before the phase 4 comparison judges it.

decisions.decision: How does the import change a shipped file?
decisions.ruling: Each shipped file keeps its content byte for byte. Only the old header line becomes the new two-line header, and each required message that named <tool>.toml now names [tools.<tool>] of macos.toml. One kind of comment edit is allowed: a comment that the import makes false changes to the new fact. In homebrew, upgrade/brew:22 and brew/casks:8 say [bootstrap.packages] in conf.d/*.toml; they now say [mise.bootstrap.packages] in tools.toml (generated into conf.d/<tool>/mise.toml). The unit reports each such edit as DECIDED. Each old .config/mise/conf.d/* fragment is not shipped: its tables move into [mise.*] of tools.toml.
decisions.rejected: Fix or reformat content during the import; the phase 4 comparison judges each difference.

decisions.decision: What happens to an empty [defaults] table?
decisions.ruling: It goes. A tools.toml has [defaults] only when it holds a value.

[mise.env] PROJECTS_DIR = "<% index .config `projects_dir` | required `cli: set projects_dir in [tools.cli] of macos.toml` | regexp.Replace `^~` .env.HOME %>". The TOML string quotes the value, so the old printf %q goes. projects_dir stays in [defaults] with the default ~/Projects.
decisions.rejected: A literal path that ignores the value.

decisions.decision: Does the plan add test cases?
decisions.ruling: No. test:macos-tools (P10) renders each new tool through macos/examples/macos.toml, and it fails when a tool folder is not selected. U2 selects diff-so-fancy in the example, because no base tool depends on it before P12.
decisions.rejected: A test case for each tool.

decisions.decision: Does the plan need a review unit?
decisions.ruling: Yes. U1 lands task scripts (cli, homebrew, node) and shell drop-ins that run on each Mac. One review unit in wave 2 covers U1 and U2.
decisions.rejected: No review unit: the wave review alone does not run /security-review.

decisions.decision: Can this plan run in parallel with another plan of the chain?
decisions.ruling: No. The 16 plans form one linear chain through requires, because most of them edit sync-engine/repo-sync or sync-engine/setup-sync, and parallel plans conflict there.

decisions.decision: Does the plan run setup:configs or the Mac sync?
decisions.ruling: No. mise run setup:configs in bootstrap and in consumers, and the first Mac run, stay hand steps (Out of scope).
decisions.rejected: A unit or an after-landing step that runs them.

decisions.ruling: [pack.essentials], as diff-so-fancy = {}, because the old default list of essentials omits it. git brings it into each Mac through depends (P12).
decisions.rejected: [pack.base], which the old packs.toml does not do.

decisions.decision: Does python.uv_venv_auto = "create|source" stay in macos/tools/python/tools.toml for this import (G5)?
decisions.ruling: User ruling 2026-11-05: yes, for this import only. D4 and R2 stand, and the value stays byte for byte, because the live Mac already has it. The risk stays until a separate plan after this run changes the value. A security review of this plan does not report this case again.
decisions.rejected: Remove source and create from the Mac default in this import.

decisions.decision: Does MISE_TRUSTED_CONFIG_PATHS keep all of projects_dir in the three mise shell templates for this import (G6)?
decisions.ruling: User ruling 2026-11-05: yes, for this import only. D4 stands, and the content stays byte for byte, because the live Mac already has it. The risk stays until a separate plan after this run changes the value. A security review of this plan does not report this case again.
decisions.rejected: Narrow the path to the owner folders in this import.

decisions.decision: Does a security finding in content that this plan imports unchanged from macos-setup stop the run (G8, G9, G10)?
decisions.ruling: User ruling 2026-11-05: no. A security finding in content that is byte for byte from macos-setup, apart from the changes that D4 and R2 name, is accepted for this import. It does not stop the run, and the content does not change. The run records each such finding as an open gap with its severity and location, for one security plan after the run. G8 and G9 are accepted under this ruling. A finding in code that this plan writes or changes stops the run as before.
decisions.rejected: Accept only G8 and G9, and stop on each new finding in imported content.

UNRESOLVED security finding [high] macos/tools/python/tools.toml:10 (U1): python.uv_venv_auto = "create|source" puts the .venv/bin of a repo on PATH with no trust check, so cd into a hostile clone with uv.lock and a committed .venv runs a planted binary as the user (tested on mise 2026.11.1 with paranoid = true). A fix changes a value that D4 and R2 keep byte for byte · ruling needed: remove source and create from the Mac default, or accept the risk. The same line is at repo/tools/python/tools.toml:21, outside this range RULING (2026-11-06-security-gaps D2): Fixed: the Mac config no longer sets uv_venv_auto; uv creates the venv at uv run.

UNRESOLVED security finding [high] macos/tools/mise/.config/zsh/01b-mise.zsh.tmpl:6, bash/01b-mise.bash.tmpl:10, fish/conf.d/06-mise.fish.tmpl:9 (U1): MISE_TRUSTED_CONFIG_PATHS holds the whole projects_dir (default ~/Projects) and cancels paranoid = true of config.toml:16, so a repo cloned there loads its mise config with no trust prompt (tested: [env] loads silently; code execution through _.source or [hooks] not tested). A fix changes content that D4 keeps byte for byte · ruling needed: narrow the path to the owner namespaces, drop projects_dir and use mise trust per repo, or accept the risk RULING (2026-11-06-security-gaps D1): Fixed: only ~/.config/mise and the github.com and gitlab.com folders are trusted.

SPEC/PLAN GAP: D4, R2 and R3 copy every value byte for byte and name no security requirement for the mise trust boundary; both values are unchanged from macos-setup, so the live Mac already has this exposure and the import carries it forward; index.json has no ruling on either · no assumption taken; G5 and G6 hold the rulings RULING (2026-11-06-security-gaps D1): Accepted: a spec gap of the import; D1 now gives the requirement.

UNRESOLVED security finding [high] macos/tools/starship/.config/starship.toml:147 (U1): the when command of custom.submodule_status runs git status on every prompt, gated only by a .gitmodules file, so an extracted tar or zip with core.fsmonitor in .git/config runs code as the owner on cd, also outside projects_dir (tested: starship prompt ran the planted hook on git 2.56; -c core.fsmonitor= stops that hook, but a filter clean driver from the repo config still ran). A plain git clone does not carry .git/config. Byte for byte from macos-setup, so the live Mac already has it. A fix changes content that D4 keeps byte for byte · accepted for this import under D14; for one security plan after the run RULING (2026-11-06-security-gaps D3): Partly fixed: the custom command runs git status only below the two folders; git_status stays, accepted.

UNRESOLVED security finding [high] macos/tools/homebrew/tools.toml:25 (U1): the brew alias fnox exec -P brew -- brew pins no config, so fnox merges a fnox.toml from the current folder and its parents with no trust gate; a committed fnox.toml with a profiles.brew PATH secret makes any brew command there run a planted binary as the owner (tested on fnox 1.47.0), and that binary receives the profile token value (tested with a scratch default value; a Keychain token is inferred). The engine rated this medium on a credential_command route that did not fire in the test; the reviewer rated it high on the PATH route. With fnox -c "$HOME/.config/fnox/config.toml" the project file did not load (tested; not tested through the generated mise alias). The value is byte for byte from macos-setup, so the live Mac already has it. A fix changes a value that R2 keeps byte for byte · accepted for this import under D14; for one security plan after the run RULING (2026-11-06-security-gaps D4): Fixed: the brew alias and updateall pin the user fnox config; CONTEXT7_RUNNER is deleted (D5).

SPEC/PLAN GAP: D4, R2 and R3 copy every value and file byte for byte and name no security requirement for prompt commands that run on cd or aliases that read current-folder config; G7 records this only for the mise trust boundary · no assumption taken; G8 and G9 hold the rulings RULING (2026-11-06-security-gaps D3): Accepted: a spec gap of the import; D3 now gives the requirement.
